Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

The ICTS Pilot Program Administrator independently manages the ICTS Pilot Studies Program with guidance from the Pilot Program Director, including creating the calls, managing and screening applications, assigning reviewers, compiling scores and analyzing the reviews, ensuring institutional and national compliance, and providing recommendations for funding. The incumbent will work with faculty and staff at all levels of leadership in the ICTS and other departments on campus.

The Pilot Program Administrator is responsible for all points of contact regarding pilot funding through the ICTS, including pre- and post-award management, including application inquiries, prior approval, local and national meetings and consortia, like CEREC (CTSA External Reviewer Exchange Consortium) and the NIH Prior Approval and Quality Assurance/Quality Control Group.

The incumbent will use their skills as a seasoned, experienced professional with a full understanding of analytical practices, policies and procedures. They will research, analyze and develop solutions to a wide range of issues, including but not limited to: Pilot Program policy development, strategic creation and implementation of grant calls, troubleshooting all aspects of the pilot award process from development to closeout. They will demonstrate good judgment in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions; primarily deal with policies, programs and proposals which are complex in nature and diverse in scope; and develop new programs, policies or procedures for possible implementation.
Strong policy analysis techniques.
Knowledge of common organization- or research-specific and other computer application programs (eg. Office Suite, REDCap, Smartsheet, Adobe Suite)

Strong communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing to successfully interact with a broad spectrum of people including faculty, staff, and members of the community from diverse cultures and backgrounds.
Strong skills in analyzing, researching and synthesizing large amounts of data for preparing sound and relevant proposals / analyses. Ability to evaluate and analyze for process improvement.

Ability to use discretion and maintain all confidentiality. Demonstrated ability to exercise good judgment, tact, diplomacy, and discretion in handling a variety of complex and highly confidential matters.

Analytical / problem-solving skills for any and all issues and concerns from faculty, staff, and community members. Able to independently accomplish tasks in an environment with changing and conflicting priorities.

Ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes.Able to work under pressure from constant deadlines. Demonstrated organizational and project management skills. Able to use independent judgement to initiate and track complex issues and projects to completion.
